Planned Investigations  
• Blood panel ordered: CBC, inflammatory markers (ESR/CRP), rheumatologic antibodies, serum urate – results pending.

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings: 53-year-old man with 1-week painless swelling over left olecranon, mild warmth, full range of motion, no systemic features. Video inspection shows localized fluctuant swelling; mild adjacent tenderness; skin slightly dry.

Working diagnosis: Aseptic (non-infectious) olecranon bursitis.

Supporting DDx information: High likelihood per DDx—classic presentation without systemic signs. Differential considerations:  
• Septic olecranon bursitis (medium likelihood) – excluded clinically at present but will review with labs and monitor for increasing pain, erythema, or systemic symptoms.  
• Gouty olecranon bursitis (medium–low likelihood) – serum urate ordered to evaluate.  

Management:  
1. Pharmacologic – Ibuprofen 400 mg PO twice daily with food; cease if gastrointestinal adverse effects.  
2. Investigations – Blood tests as above; forms mailed to patient.  
3. Safety-net – Education on red-flag symptoms (increasing pain, redness, spreading erythema, severe tenderness, fever); advised urgent review if these occur.  
4. Follow-up – Arrange review (video or in-person) ~6 days after blood draw to assess clinical progress and review results.

Health Promotion & Planning

- Education on chronic disease prevention and lifestyle modification: Provided advice regarding NSAID use and monitoring for infection; broader preventive education not recorded.  
- Patient health goals and priorities: Not recorded  
- Eligibility for GP Management Plan (GPMP) or Team Care Arrangements (TCA): Not recorded  
- Referrals (allied health, Quitline, AOD services, Aboriginal health worker, or social supports): Laboratory referral for blood tests issued.  
- Follow-up and recall appointments scheduled: Patient to schedule follow-up after blood tests; urgent review if symptoms worsen.  

Consider

- Mental health support or counselling referral: Not recorded  
- Specialist referral for complex chronic disease management: Consider rheumatology referral if atypical findings or recurrent bursitis after evaluation.  
- Dental referral if oral health issues identified: Not recorded  
- Optometry referral for visual concerns or regular screening: Not recorded  
- Audiometry referral if hearing issues suspected: Not recorded  
- Social work or housing support referral if social determinants affect health: Not recorded  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

1. Aseptic (non-infectious) olecranon bursitis – High likelihood; painless localized swelling with minimal tenderness and preserved joint function, no systemic features.  
2. Septic olecranon bursitis – Medium likelihood; warmth and mild tenderness warrant exclusion through observation and labs.  
3. Gouty olecranon bursitis – Low-medium likelihood; middle-aged male, will assess serum urate; no prior gout attacks reported.

● Missing but clinically expected elements: vitals, anthropometry (height/weight/BMI), smoking/alcohol history, diet, immunisation review (flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus), cardiovascular and metabolic screening (BP, glucose, lipids), urinalysis.  
● Internal conflicts or contradictions: None noted between transcript and DDx.  
● Transcript quality notes: Audio clear; limited scope—focused chiefly on elbow complaint; preventive health domains largely unaddressed.
